Definition: something that rises, i.e. a stalk of grain
BiblicalUsage: Standing corn is the crop still in the field: a neighbour may pluck the ears with his hand but not put a sickle to it, Samson burnt up the standing corn of the Philistines with the shocks and the vineyards, and Hosea says they have sown the wind and shall reap the whirlwind, for it hath no stalk.
TheologicalSignificance: I read the standing corn as the harvest before it is gathered, and the place where mercy and judgment meet.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
